title: Declassified documents suggest Catalina Island was hot spot for UFO sightings

content:
Newly declassified documents suggest a popular tourist destination off the coast of Southern California was once a hot spot for UFO sightings.

Details on a string of alleged UFO sightings near Catalina Island were released by the White House in a Friday morning document dump concerning unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UAPs.

Several sightings are detailed in the documents, which date back as far as the late 1940s.

One report describes an encounter in August 1952 by a group of Boy Scouts who said they saw an “object silver in color” that moved “faster than a conventional jet” while hiking near Camp Fox at noon.

The Boy Scouts were unable to determine the object’s altitude, speed or distance, according to the report. The object reportedly climbed quickly before disintegrating.

According to the California Post, the biggest mystery surrounding the alleged sighting may be a missing sketch of the object. The sketch was reportedly drawn on the back of the original report but remains unaccounted for, despite searches of government archives.

Another document, a handwritten note from an Avalon man to an acquaintance in Boise, Idaho, dated May 1, 1947, describes another alleged sighting.

The letter said, “About 8 o’clock of the night of April 28th, my wife and a school teacher saw six objects in the sky, not in a group, but singly. A few minutes later after going to my daughter’s home, on the next street and corresponding block, she and my daughter and my grandson saw four more. All traveling in the same direction.”

A handwritten annotation indicates that the U.S. Air Force concluded the incident “lacked sufficient data for evaluation.”

Another report from November 1953 describes a “round, purplish-white object” above Catalina Island that remained stationary, then moved “northwest toward Los Angeles over approximately 10 minutes on a level flight path.”

The report characterized the observer as fairly reliable due to his association with military jet aircraft activities while stationed at Long Beach Air Force Base.

An assessment by a local astronomer said that “Jupiter provided a possible explanation.”

The final document details a civilian’s March 1955 sighting of an object that was “approximately the size of a nickel held at arm’s length, very bright and orange and color” and appeared to fall straight down in the vicinity of Catalina Island.

An assessment included in the report says the sighting “is possible astronomical,” but no further investigation was deemed worthwhile.

The records are part of the Trump administration’s effort to release files concerning UAPs through its Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters initiative.

Friday’s release is the seventh of its kind from the White House, according to the U.S. Department of War website. The first round of documents was released on May 8.

You can see them on the Department of War website.
